Car Accident Lawyer for Pasadena

Pasadena sits where the 210, the 134, and the 110 (Arroyo Seco Parkway) meet. Add Old Pasadena's crowds, Caltech and PCC traffic, and Rose Bowl events, and crashes are a daily reality. Prospect Law Group's Glendale office is a short drive west on the 134, and we represent injured people throughout Pasadena.

Attorney Vardan Daldumyan is a former in-house trial attorney for an insurance company. He uses what he learned on the inside to build claims insurers take seriously.

Free consultation. No fee unless we recover.

Where Pasadena Crashes Happen

  • Colorado Boulevard, through Old Pasadena and the Playhouse District, with pedestrians and frequent stops
  • Lake Avenue and Arroyo Parkway, with heavy shopping and commuter traffic
  • The Arroyo Seco Parkway (110), with tight curves, short on-ramps, and almost no shoulder
  • The 210/134 interchange, with constant merging traffic
  • Rose Bowl and Arroyo Seco area, during game days and events

What to Do After a Pasadena Crash

  1. Call 911. Pasadena Police generally handle city streets; CHP handles the freeways.
  2. Photograph the vehicles, the scene, and your injuries.
  3. Exchange insurance and license information.
  4. See a doctor promptly.
  5. Do not give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer.
  6. Call us.

Full checklist: What to do after a car accident in California

Frequently Asked Questions

Who takes the police report for a Pasadena crash?

Pasadena Police Department typically handles crashes on city streets. Crashes on the 210, 134, or 110 are generally handled by the California Highway Patrol.

What if I was hurt in traffic around a Rose Bowl event?

Event traffic, temporary lane closures, and crowds raise crash risk. Your claim works like any other car accident claim, but if a government-controlled road condition contributed, a six-month claim deadline may apply.
